criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: Clear structure with headings and contents; figures labelled. But references are bare URLs without titles/authors, Wikipedia used (explicitly disallowed), some garbled sentences ('which is also desirable' for low resolution), and figure captions inconsistent.

technical_issues.issue: Sun-synchronous inclination at 600 km should be ~97.8° (retrograde, >90°), not 87.79°; contradicts their own inclination-vs-altitude plot and the stated 'retrograde' orbit.
Kourou's latitude stated as 45.05°N; it is ~5.2°N. The claim that two launch windows occur daily because latitude is smaller than target inclination is built on this error.
RAAN of 27.33° said to 'indicate the location of the launch facility' — RAAN is not directly set by launch site longitude without further argument.
Contradictory statement: 'A very high altitude would yield low resolution images which is also desirable' — low resolution is not desirable.
Contradictory: satellite described as 'without thrusters' yet earlier an orbital manoeuvre at EOL is mentioned; drag sail choice is consistent but reasoning is muddled.

overall: Well-structured report addressing nearly all task requirements with STK evidence, but undermined by a fundamental orbital-mechanics error (SSO inclination), a factual launch-site error, weak referencing (bare URLs, Wikipedia), and vague user identification. Adequate-to-good overall; core mission design logic is otherwise reasonable.

feedback.summary: A well-structured report addressing nearly all requirements with good STK evidence (screenshots, access reports, ground tracks). However, a fundamental orbital-mechanics error (SSO inclination), a factual launch-site error, weak referencing, and vague user identification hold the mark at Adequate. Fixing these specific issues would lift the design work substantially.
next_steps: Correct the sun-synchronous inclination at 600 km to ~97.8° (retrograde, >90°) and reconcile it with your own inclination-vs-altitude plot and orbit description.
Fix the Kourou latitude (~5.2°N, not 45.05°N) and rebuild the launch-window argument on the corrected value; clarify how RAAN relates to launch site longitude.

Replace bare URLs and Wikipedia with proper citations (author, title, year) and ensure every in-text citation matches the reference list; explicitly name the operator and customer groups in the Introduction.

criteria.C1: You clearly state the primary mission, justify its need for Australian coral-bleaching monitoring, and give a solid single-spacecraft rationale (simplicity, cost, communications). To reach Accomplished, explicitly identify the operator and the customers — 'operated and accessed from Australian ground facilities' is too vague; name who owns, runs, and buys the data, with supporting references.
criteria.C2: All major requirements are addressed with good STK evidence, including a ~20-minute average contact duration and clear launch/EOL discussion. However, key errors undermine persuasiveness: the SSO inclination at 600 km should be ~97.8° (retrograde), not 87.79°, contradicting your own plot; Kourou's latitude is ~5.2°N, not 45.05°N, invalidating your launch-window reasoning; RAAN does not directly indicate launch-site location; and 'low resolution... is also desirable' contradicts your imaging goal. Also resolve the thruster-vs-EOL-manoeuvre contradiction. Correcting these and tightening the design logic would move you to Accomplished.
criteria.C3: Your conclusions are specific and evidence-based, including honest risk acknowledgement (Vega E not yet built) and fallback options — well done. To strengthen further, extend the same specificity to the other mission segments (orbit, ground segment) rather than focusing mainly on launch risk.
criteria.C4: The report has clear structure, headings, contents, and labelled figures. To reach Accomplished: replace bare URLs and Wikipedia (not permitted) with full citations (author, title, year) matched to in-text references; fix garbled sentences such as the low-resolution contradiction; and make figure captions and formatting consistent throughout.
